title: The quiet log
bodyMd:
A fictional software team installed an alert system that reported every unusual event. Within days, the channel carried hundreds of messages, most caused by harmless variations. Important failures were still reported, but engineers sometimes missed them among the routine alerts. One proposal was to disable the system altogether. Instead, the team grouped repeated messages and assigned different levels of urgency.

The total number of alerts fell. The team treated this neither as proof that the software had become more reliable nor as evidence that fewer events occurred. The reporting rules had changed. To judge reliability, it separately tracked service interruptions and recovery time. To judge the alert system, it examined whether engineers received and acted on significant warnings in time. These were related questions, but they were not the same question.
